item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q012_not_true_family_specific_pair","answer":"No—not in the evolutionary sense. In SCOPe 2.08, d1s9za_ and d1hqja_ share SCCS k.40.1.1 and family sunid 100905 (“Designed trimeric coiled-coil”), as well as the corresponding superfamily and fold. However, both are synthetic de novo designs: 1s9z is an amyloidogenic 17-residue coiled-coil peptide, whereas 1hqj is a designed trimeric coiled-coil. Here the shared family reflects structural/design similarity, not demonstrated descent from a biological common ancestor. Therefore amyloidogenicity or other functional properties must not be transferred between them without direct experimental evidence, and neither should be treated as an evolutionary representative or homology-modeling template for the other solely from this classification. A claim of a specific design lineage would require external sequence and design-provenance evidence.","evidence_used":["/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d1s9za_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d1hqja_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/98768","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/61142","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/103786","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/64668","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/103785","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/100906","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/100905","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/100904","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/100903","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/58788","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1s9z","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1hqj"]}]}
